full_judgment:
Mustafa Kamal, J. : The pre-emptor-petitioner obtained an ex parte decree for pre-emption in Miscellaneous Case No.20 of 1985 from the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Gazipur on 6-7-86 and took possession of the case property through Court on 8-8-86. The pre-emptee respondents filed an application under order IX Rule 13 C.P.C. for setting aside the ex parte judgment and order dated 6-7-86, Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1986. The pre-emptor-petitioner contested the same by filing a written objection. By judgment and order dated 27-2-90 the trial Court dismissed Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1986. The pre-emptee-respondents mistakenly filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of. 1990 before the learned District Judge, Gazipur against the said judgment and order dated 27-2-90. The learned Additional District Judge, Gazipur by his judgment and order dated 30-6-93 dis-missed the said Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 1990 against which the pre-emptee-respondents preferred Civil Revision No.2874 of 1993 in which the Rule was made absolute by a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division by judgment and order dated 22-7-97. 

 3. Mr. M.A. Wahhab Miah, learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the learned Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in treating the revisional application as one against the judgment and order of the trial Court dated 27-2-90 in Miscellaneous Case No.4 of 1986. 

 4. The High Court Division rightly found that the pre-emptee-respondents' appeal was misconceived and inadvertent and that in revisional jurisdiction the Court was competent to examine the order dated 27-2-90 passed by the trial Court. We do not think that the learned Judge of the High Court Division committed any error of law in taking that view. 

 5. Mr. M.A. Wahhab Miah next submits that the summons of the original pre-emption case was served on the husband of the pre-emptee respondent who said in her evidence that, her husband looks after her property. In that view of the matter, he submits, the learned Judge of the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that the summons was not duly served upon the pre-emptee-respondent. 

 6. The High Court Division rightly held that in the instant case there is no evidence that the husband of the pre-emptee respondent was the recognised agent of hers. Therefore the summons was not duly served upon the pre .emptee respondent. Limitation will start from the date of knowledge which is 8-8-86 and the pre-emptee respondent filed Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 1986 on 11-8-86 well within the period of limitation as prescribed by Article 164 of the First Schedule to the Limitation Act.
